entries.topic: World layer of the 1948 network: foreign governments before 1948 (France 1917, Poland 1937-39, Smuts), the 1944 platforms, UNSCOP, the French arms for the Altalena (Nov 2026)
claims: 13 Jan 1922: Sokolow met Harding for nearly an hour during the Keren Hayesod tour (whether it touched the resolution is not recorded).
Taft chaired the Republican Resolutions Committee and invited Silver to give the convention benediction; the GOP plank called for "unrestricted immigration and land ownership".
Silver had a close relationship with Taft and lobbied Republican leaders on the plank.
Celler sat on the Democratic Resolutions Committee and backed Wise's push for a stronger plank; he warned the White House of Jewish voters' anger over the White Paper.
Wise lobbied Democratic delegates in Chicago for a plank to match the Republicans'.
Wise secured a meeting with Roosevelt, who weakened the Palestine statement Wise had drafted.
Rep. Emanuel Celler of Brooklyn, a leading House supporter.
Sol Bloom chaired the House Foreign Affairs Committee and was a leading supporter.
Other account: the charter firm Service Airways Inc. was the cover.
Charles Winters exported B-17 bombers (two or three by different accounts).
Convicted under the Neutrality Act (1949); served 18 months; pardoned posthumously (2008, Bush; another account says 2001, Clinton).
Secret agreement approved by Foreign Minister Bidault: weapons worth 153 million francs for the Altalena, sailed from Port-de-Bouc 11 June 1948 (text of the agreement not found; motives unclear).
Georges Bidault, French Foreign Minister.
The Irgun's arms ship (about 940 volunteers).
Guatemala's UN ambassador and UNSCOP member.
Organized a lobby of Central and South American states for partition.
First Latin American state to recognize Israel.
June 1917: the French diplomat Jules Cambon wrote of "the renaissance of the Jewish nationality in that Land", months before Balfour.
Addressed to Nahum Sokolow.
A statement of French government sympathy (unpublished at the time).
Martin Kramer argues French assent, with the Vatican's, was a precondition for Balfour.
1936: Jabotinsky met Polish Foreign Minister Józef Beck and laid a basis for cooperation (Irgun's own history).
Józef Beck, Polish Foreign Minister.
Nov 1937: Avraham Stern met senior officials in Warsaw to arrange army-Irgun cooperation.

1937-39: weapons from Polish army depots were shipped to Palestine; Polish officers in civilian clothes trained Irgun commanders (Carpathians, 25 Mar 1939). Warsaw hoped a Jewish state would draw Jewish emigration from Poland.
Stern, then of the Irgun (later founder of Lehi).
Member of Britain's Imperial War Cabinet; helped formulate the Balfour Declaration and the Mandate.
A personal friend of Weizmann and long-standing supporter.
Prime Minister of South Africa.
1948: Smuts's government quickly granted de facto recognition, shortly before losing the election.
